stories.headline: LAC must be stable for normalisation of ties with China: Jaishankar
stories.title: LAC must be stable for normalisation of ties with China: Jaishankar
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14: The Line of Actual Control (LAC) has to be stable for normalising relations between India and China, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said, asserting that any disturbance along the border will have consequences. Jaishankar also linked expansion of trade and investment ties between the two countries to peace and tranquillity along the border. "The point we make to the Chinese is: 'If you want a normal relationship, if the rest of the relationship is to move, it's common sense -- It is a no-brainer that the boundary has to be stable and that we need peace and tranquillity in the border areas'," he said. Jaishankar, speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Tuesday evening, noted that the situation along the LAC has "settled down" to a great extent since 2024 and that the relationship is "commensurately moving towards normalcy." In the last few months, both sides have rolled out a series of confidence-building measures to repair ties frayed by the more than four-and-a-half-year military standoff in eastern Ladakh. The face-off ended in late 2024. To a question on whether India would allow more Chinese investment in the country in case there was an "early harvest" agreement on the boundary question, Jaishankar broadly said that various possibilities are being looked at. "We are now looking at those possibilities, and we have to see where we go. But we are not insisting that you have to solve the boundary issue in order to do business." "What we are saying is: the bar is lower. The bar is: maintain peace and tranquillity. I wouldn't link the early harvest to anything other than the boundary question resolution. Anything we do on any policy we have on business, market access issues will be dealt with separately." The external affairs minister also flagged concerns over economic issues with China. "We also have very major economic issues with China. If you look today at the trade balance, it is completely tilted (towards China)," he said. "The tilt is extremely one-sided, and in many sectors where we have done well with the rest of the world, we have not had market access; we have not had a successful business operation for that sector in China," he said. "We do believe today that we're not getting a level playing field in China in the manner in which we have given a level playing field to them," he noted. Jaishankar also referred to the Galwan valley clashes of 2020 and explained how it brought the ties under severe strain. "From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said. "Then in 2020, when we were in the midst of the Covid lockdown, we had a series of border issues, and it culminated in a clash in which a number of soldiers were killed on either side," he said. "For us, what it represented was a very profound departure from the situation that was prevailing since 1975. If the peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences," he said. Jaishankar said those consequences were very visible in the next few years until peace and tranquillity was restored.

stories.headline: DRI busts illegal import of over 73,00,000 kg of Pakistan-origin rock salt; 4 arrested
stories.title: DRI busts illegal import of over 73,00,000 kg of Pakistan-origin rock salt; 4 arrested
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has once again unearthed a large-scale scheme to circumvent India’s prohibition on the import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan under “Operation Deep Manifest”. DRI detected the import of 295 containers carrying 7,311 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin Industrial/Himalayan Rock Salt, with an estimated market value of around Rs. 30 crore. The consignments were routed through Colombo Port, Sri Lanka, and falsifying their origin by using fabricated certificates of origin and invoices issued by UAE-based entities. Acting on specific intelligence, DRI launched a coordinated, fortnight-long operation between 26 September and 11 October 2026, conducting searches at linked premises in Gandhidham, Adipur, Veraval, Panipat, Pune, Patiala, Delhi and Mumbai. Investigation revealed that nine importers had brought in the 295 containers through Mundra and Kandla ports since March 2026, in violation of the prohibition. Out of the total 295 containers detected, five containers carrying 140 MT of Industrial/Himalayan Rock Salt, valued at Rs. 24.41 lakh, have been seized at Kandla Port. In addition, sales proceeds amounting to Rs. 20.96 lakh held in the importers’ bank accounts have been seized. Preliminary investigation has uncovered a transnational network involving entities owned by Pakistani, UAE, Sri Lankan and Indian nationals. The network allegedly coordinated the shipments and supporting documentation to disguise the Pakistani origin of the goods. Fabricated invoices issued by Dubai-based firms were used to support the transactions. Significantly, Bills of Lading relating to the Pakistan–Sri Lanka leg of the shipments and customs declarations filed with Sri Lanka Customs expressly mentioned Pakistan as the country of origin and India as the final destination. The Certificates of Origin submitted by the importers were found to be fabricated. Four persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962: two proprietors/partners of importing firms, a Customs Broker’s G-card holder, and the owner of a Dubai-based supplier who had also established and operated an importing firm in his father’s name. In a similar crackdown last month, DRI seized over 362,000 kg of Pakistan-origin dry dates packed in 13 containers imported by a Mumbai-based firm at CFS Ambad, Nashik. These cases highlight the evolving methods used by transnational networks to circumvent India’s import prohibition on Pakistani origin goods through third-country routing, false declarations of origin, fabricated trade documents and opaque financial arrangements. DRI remains committed to identifying and dismantling such networks and safeguarding India’s economic and national security interests. Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, the Government of India imposed a complete prohibition on the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, in the interest of national security and public policy, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 02.05.2025.

stories.headline: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush Goyal
stories.title: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush Goyal
stories.summary: India does not see any problems in its agreements with the United States, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday, playing down any suggestion that ties depend on who occupies the White House.Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Goyal was asked whether relations would improve after the tenure of the current US president. He said they were already “very good”. “I don’t see any problem in any agreements with the United States. It’s about trade, defence partnership, technology partnership, it’s our critical maintenance partnership and our people-to-people engagement,” he said, adding that Washington is India’s largest trading partner and will remain so in the years ahead.The relationship, Goyal said, will strengthen “irrespective of changes in political thinking” in either country. Drawing on economic, political and security imperatives, it is “a very safe relationship” that the rest of the world need not worry about, he added.Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau as FM flags tough road ahead“I think the US and India have a very consequential relationship, and it’s only going to get better, irrespective of changes in political thinking, whether in India or in the US,” the commerce minister said further.Goyal said the pandemic exposed India’s vulnerability when critical supplies, including vaccines, failed to arrive. That experience prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for a self-sufficient India, including a push into semiconductors, given annual chip purchases of $130 billion to $150 billion.Self-reliance did not mean isolation, he stressed. India has signed preferential trade agreements with 38 developed nations in the past four and a half years, he said, raising the GDP covered by such pacts to $70 trillion from $10 trillion before 2014. Talks are under way with Canada, Mexico, the Gulf Cooperation Council, Eurasia, Mercosur, the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) and others, which could take coverage to about $85 trillion of a $115 trillion global total.Also Read: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?Trust was the key ingredient, he said, describing India’s aim as “a fair mix of efficiency amongst friends and self-sufficiency for critical elements”. India is now largely self-sufficient in food and energy, he said.On China, Goyal said India was open to engagement provided it gets a fair deal, continuity and geopolitical stability, adding that “the last word has not yet been scripted.”

Drawing on economic, political and security imperatives, it is “a very safe relationship” that the rest of the world need not worry about, he added.

“I think the US and India have a very consequential relationship, and it’s only going to get better, irrespective of changes in political thinking, whether in India or in the US,” the commerce minister said further.

That experience prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for a self-sufficient India, including a push into semiconductors, given annual chip purchases of $130 billion to $150 billion.

India has signed preferential trade agreements with 38 developed nations in the past four and a half years, he said, raising the GDP covered by such pacts to $70 trillion from $10 trillion before 2014.

Talks are under way with Canada, Mexico, the Gulf Cooperation Council, Eurasia, Mercosur, the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) and others, which could take coverage to about $85 trillion of a $115 trillion global total..
India is now largely self-sufficient in food and energy, he said.
On China, Goyal said India was open to engagement provided it gets a fair deal, continuity and geopolitical stability, adding that “the last word has not yet been scripted.”

stories.headline: Sebi bars Rajesh Mehta from trading in Rajesh Exports, keeps curbs in place
stories.title: Sebi bars Rajesh Mehta from trading in Rajesh Exports, keeps curbs in place
stories.summary: In a confirmatory order, the market regulator demands full compliance with a forensic audit following allegations of a ₹15.15-trillion revenue misrepresentation between FY21 and FY25.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'sebi bars' in title weight 42
event term: 'market regulator' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has backed its restrictions on Rajesh Exports Ltd and its managing director Rajesh Mehta, directing them to cooperate with an ongoing investigation into the company’s financial disclosures and transactions, while barring Mehta from dealing in the company’s securities until further orders.
In a confirmatory order issued on Wednesday, Sebi said the company and Mehta must provide documents, information and explanations sought by the investigating authority.

Rajesh Exports must also ensure truthful, accurate and complete disclosures in its financial statements, related-party transactions and other material information under applicable securities regulations.
The regulator directed a newly appointed forensic auditor to complete its work expeditiously and asked the investigating authority to conclude its probe without delay.
The directions took immediate effect and will remain in force until further orders.
The order follows an interim order dated 3 June, which raised concerns over the company’s financial reporting, disclosures and cooperation with the investigation.
The regulator said its prima facie findings indicate that Rajesh Exports overstated and misrepresented the group’s operational scale and financial performance between FY21 and FY25.
It alleged that about ₹15.15 trillion, or 99.8% of revenue attributed to the company’s subsidiaries during the period, was misrepresented.
The order flagged a significant disparity between Rajesh Exports’ consolidated revenue and the standalone revenue reported by its Swiss subsidiary, Valcambi SA.
For the five-year period from financial year 2020-21 to 2024-25, the company’s consolidated revenue was ₹15.45 trillion, while Valcambi’s standalone revenue was ₹3,027.38 crore.

Sebi said the difference raised concerns about the verifiability and reliability of the consolidated financial disclosures considering that about 97-99% of the company’s consolidated revenue was reported to originate from overseas subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries.
Sebi also flagged inconsistencies in submissions made during the investigation.

stories.headline: Supreme Court questions Chhattisgarh HC relief in 2021 murder case
stories.title: Supreme Court questions Chhattisgarh HC relief in 2021 murder case
stories.summary: Supreme Court questions Chhattisgarh HC relief in 2021 murder case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court questioned the reduction of Chintamani Patel's murder conviction and issued notices.
The scrutiny could result in restoration of the trial court's life sentence.
The Supreme Court has expressed displeasure over a Chhattisgarh High Court verdict that reduced the conviction of a man from murder to culpable homicide and cut his life sentence to 10 years.

A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran issued notices to the state government and the accused, Chintamani alias Chintu Patel, asking why the High Court order should not be set aside and the trial court's murder conviction restored.
Referring to the High Court's November 29, 2024 order, the bench said, "Just see the pathetic condition of the high court.
The judges don't know what Section 304 Part I and 304 Part II of the IPC are.
You expect the judges to appreciate the evidence."
Section 304 Part I of the Indian Penal Code deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder when there is an intention to cause death or an injury likely to cause death.
Part II applies when a person knows that an act is likely to cause death but has no intention to cause it.
Chintamani, through his legal-aid counsel, argued that there was no evidence against him and that the High Court had erred in its findings.
Justice Pardiwala told the counsel, "This is not the first judgment of this kind we are coming across.
These are all principles of law which law schools teach in the very first year of the academic session itself."

article_sentences: The Supreme Court asked the Centre to examine compensation for crops damaged by elephants.
The move links livelihood relief with efforts to keep interstate elephant corridors unobstructed.
The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked the Centre to examine compensation for crop damage caused by human-elephant conflict while hearing a petition concerning elephant corridors across states.
The court also gave the Centre more time to submit a comprehensive report on obstructions in elephant corridors and measures taken to ensure the animals can move without hindrance.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was hearing the plea in New Delhi.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati referred to the court's August 17 order directing the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change to conduct a fresh survey and submit a comprehensive report on steps taken to prevent obstructions in elephant corridors.
Bhati told the bench that the ministry had received information from some states and sought more time to file the report.
Counsel for the petitioners raised the issue of compensation.
"This relates to the human-elephant conflict and one of the main issues is compensation for crop damage, etc," the lawyer said.
"You examine this aspect," the bench told Bhati.
On August 17, the Supreme Court had directed the ministry to survey whether any state had constructed obstacles or created blockades in elephant corridors.
The bench had made it clear that states could not obstruct elephant pathways to prevent the loss of crops and livelihoods.

stories.title: Delhi protests: Metro was ‘fully functional’, 32 lakh rode trains on October 10: DMRC tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: Admits commuter traffic ‘slightly lower’ than usual second-Saturday count of 58 lakh, says protests may have dampened people’s willingness to travel

article_sentences: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) and its chairperson filed separate affidavits in the Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 15, 2026), stating that the Metro network remained “fully functional” on October 10, recording 32 lakh passengers.
“There was zero reduction in the total volume of metro operation or the number of train trips,” the DMRC said.

Though the DMRC admitted that commuter traffic was “slightly lower” than the typical 58 lakh passengers on a “normal” second Saturday, it attributed the drop to public caution amid protests rather than administrative paralysis.
It said ordinary citizens were “compelled to forgo their usual day-to-day activities” on October 10.

Crucially, of the 45 stations where entry and exit gates were regulated, 14 key interchange stations (including major transit hubs such as Rajiv Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Central Secretariat, Mandi House, Hauz Khas, Dilli Haat-INA, and Netaji Subhash Place) continued to provide full and uninterrupted line-interchange facilities for commuters.
Commuters entering the city as well as inside the city were able to change transit corridors seamlessly without disruption, the affidavit said.
“For the limited stations where passenger gates were regulated, other Metro stations had remained open to minimise inconvenience to the travelling public,” the affidavit noted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Deletes Direction Requiring Trial Courts To Seek Mitigating, Aggravating Factors In All Cases Where Death Penalty Can Be Imposed
stories.title: Supreme Court Deletes Direction Requiring Trial Courts To Seek Mitigating, Aggravating Factors In All Cases Where Death Penalty Can Be Imposed
stories.summary: Court accepted NALSA’s submission that trial courts do not contemplate imposing death penalty in all such cases.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Court accepted NALSA’s submission that trial courts do not contemplate imposing death penalty in all such cases.

The Supreme Court has deleted a direction issued on April 27 requiring trial courts to call for reports on aggravating and mitigating circumstances in every case involving an offence punishable with death, accepting the National Legal Services Authority's (NALSA) submission that the requirement would create difficulties.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order on October 7 while allowing NALSA's application seeking clarification of the April 27 directions.

The April 27 order was passed after the Court expressed concern that reports on aggravating and mitigating circumstances were often not obtained at the trial stage or during the High Court's consideration of a death reference.

Consequently, crucial information relevant to sentencing was being collected for the first time when the cases reached the Supreme Court, resulting in avoidable delays and undermining a balanced sentencing process.
The Court had directed that such reports be called for at the trial stage after conviction and before determination of sentence.
If the reports had not been called for or placed on record before the trial court, the High Court was required to obtain them at the stage of admission of the death reference.

NALSA subsequently approached the Supreme Court seeking clarification, arguing that the requirement to obtain reports in every case involving an offence punishable with death could create procedural difficulties.
Advocate Rashmi Nandakumar, appearing for NALSA, submitted that there could be several cases in which the trial court did not even contemplate imposing a death sentence.
Nevertheless, the April 27 directions would require the court to undertake the exercise of calling for reports on aggravating and mitigating circumstances.
NALSA also pointed out that trial courts might lack the resources and facilities necessary to undertake such an extensive exercise.
Accepting the submission, the court held, “We are in agreement with the submission of Ms. Nandakumar.

stories.headline: Supreme Court stays Rahul Gandhi defamation trial over PM Modi remarks
stories.title: Supreme Court stays Rahul Gandhi defamation trial over PM Modi remarks
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday stayed the trial court proceedings against the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, in a criminal defamation case over his alleged ‘Chowkidar Chor Hai’ remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh also issued notice to the Maharashtra government and complainant MH Shrishrimal, seeking their responses in four weeks.
Gandhi’s plea challenged the September 8 Bombay High Court order refusing to quash the defamation case.
A defamation case was filed against the Congress leader over his 2018 remarks targeting the Prime Minister in connection with the Rafale fighter jet deal.
“Issue notice.
Returnable in four weeks.
Stay on trial,” the bench ordered.
Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi appeared for the Raebareli MP.
The case stems from a complaint filed by BJP member Mahesh Shrishrimal, who alleged that Gandhi made defamatory remarks against Modi at a rally in Rajasthan in September 2018.
The High Court had dismissed Gandhi’s petition against a Girgaon Magistrate’s order of August 28, 2019, for a proceeding against him on Shrishrimal’s complaint.

stories.headline: Lieutenant Governor congratulates GMC Srinagar on Advancing Internal Medicine Conference
stories.title: Lieutenant Governor congratulates GMC Srinagar on Advancing Internal Medicine Conference
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 14: The Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha today congratulated Government Medical College, Srinagar for organising a conference on “Advancing Internal Medicine: From Evidence to Excellence in Clinical Practice”. In his message, the Lieutenant Governor underscored the critical role of internal medicine in delivering holistic and patient-centric healthcare. The Lieutenant Governor said that physicians often face the challenging task of identifying complex underlying health conditions from seemingly simple symptoms. He noted that the strength of internal medicine lies in its ability to view the human body as an interconnected system and to understand the complete medical story of a patient through clinical knowledge, experience and careful observation. The Lieutenant Governor also stated that observation, reason, human understanding and courage remain the defining qualities of a physician. He highlighted that physicians frequently serve as the first point of medical contact for families and, in many cases, build enduring relationships across generations, rooted in trust, compassion and scientific evidence. The Lieutenant Governor in his message lauded Government Medical College, Srinagar for its significant contribution to medical education and healthcare, noting that generations of doctors trained by the institution continue to serve across Jammu Kashmir and the country. The Lieutenant Governor also highlighted the emerging healthcare challenges. “While infectious diseases remain a concern, lifestyle-related disorders such as diabetes, hypertension, obesity, fatty liver disease and cardiovascular ailments are assuming epidemic proportions. We need to ensure that advances in diagnostics, therapeutics and medical technologies reach physicians and patients in rural and remote areas as effectively as they do in urban centres,” he said. The Lieutenant Governor also called upon the medical fraternity to strengthen indigenous research and generate evidence relevant to India’s diverse population. He said that the country’s demographic diversity, combined with the expertise and commitment of doctors, presents immense opportunities for scientific discovery and innovation. “Medical science is making historic advances, and new drugs and diagnostic tools have opened up new possibilities for treatment. The greatest need today is to ensure that these innovations are not available only to physicians in large cities, but also reach doctors in villages. We must ensure that there is not even the slightest gap between urban and rural areas in access to facilities and available tools. This should be the first objective of this conference,” he said. The Lieutenant Governor also outlined a five-year roadmap and proposed six key commitments for the medical community including expanding access to advanced medical knowledge through digital health platforms and telemedicine, prioritising preventive healthcare and early detection of diseases, using technology and artificial intelligence as supportive tools while preserving clinical judgement, continuously strengthening research capacity, ensuring the wellbeing of doctors and addressing professional burnout and preserving human compassion at the centre of healthcare delivery. The Lieutenant Governor also urged the young doctors to remain curious, embrace innovation and learn from experienced mentors. He also called upon senior physicians to generously share their clinical wisdom and guide the next generation of healthcare professionals. “Early detection of diabetes, hypertension and liver disease is less costly and can help reduce treatment expenses. I urge all physicians and internists to lead prevention campaigns at the community level, because a doctor’s voice can have an extraordinary influence on society. I have every confidence that people will take your advice seriously when it comes to preventing lifestyle-related diseases. We must value physicians’ hard work, service and dedication. Along with caring for patients, hospitals and institutions, it should be ensured that doctors are cared for too. Providing them with better workplaces and working conditions should be a priority,” the Lieutenant Governor said.
